human_economic_burden.boundary: The cost value is a source-reported continuing cleanup-cost lower bound; reported symptoms are retained as context and do not add separate score points.

extent.boundary: Affected river miles document the case footprint; the normalized extent component uses represented countries so a regional case is not treated as global coverage.

source_locators: What Happened: 843,444 gallons released, cleanup costs exceeding USD 767 million, and about 320 people reporting symptoms consistent with crude-oil exposure.
Incident summary: Enbridge revised the discharge estimate to 20,082 barrels or 843,444 gallons; EPA-directed cleanup covered over 30 miles of the Kalamazoo River.
Incident and response summary: EPA-ordered recovery and dredging continued from 2010 to 2014.
Response timeline: the release traveled at least 35 miles downstream on the Kalamazoo River.

transformations.formula: Use the official revised 843,444-gallon release estimate; do not infer discharged volume from pipeline throughput, vessel capacity, traffic or risk.
Use the NTSB continuing cleanup-cost value of more than USD 767 million as a conservative numeric lower bound; do not inflate it to a final total cost.
Calculate four years from the EPA-documented 2010 through 2014 recovery-and-dredging period; do not claim ecological recovery ended in 2014.
Normalize the one represented country while retaining the at-least-35-mile river footprint as unscored context.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The released-volume estimate was revised after the incident and is retained at the official 843,444-gallon value. The USD 767 million figure was already a continuing-cost lower bound when the NTSB adopted its report, not a final total-damage valuation. The four-year duration is the documented EPA recovery-and-dredging period and does not imply that all ecological effects ended in 2014. One-country coverage prevents this severe case from being represented as a global incident census.
receipts.freshness: Historical spill assessed through 2014; federal response page reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: NTSB, PHMSA and EPA records quantify an actual inland-waterway oil discharge, continuing cleanup cost, a multi-year cleanup period, affected river length and bounded geography for the same named incident.
higher_priority_failures: The evidence is a severe regional accumulated-impact case, not a current global inland-waterway spill aggregation.
No method-comparable 20-year annual or 60-month global series supplies current magnitude plus threshold or momentum coverage.
